title: Rivermark Finance — inference intake log
body:
Quick capture from 2026-03-02 intake call (Rivermark Finance product + infra leads).

Attendees: 
- Rivermark: Nora Patel (PM), Jason Wu (Platform Eng), Derek Laube (Security)
- Redwood: Elena Park (SE, owner), Miguel Ortiz (Private deploy lead), Priya Nair (SRE cover)

Tone: conservative infra-first; they want deterministic throughput and auditability. Budget-conscious but cannot use our hosted API due to data residency and KMS constraints. They floated on-prem or VPC Private deployment.

Highlights / requirements they repeatedly emphasized:
1) Data residency & encryption
   - All inference data must never traverse public internet; must be inside their AWS account (VPC).
   - KMS integration mandatory: customer-managed CMKs, HSM-backed preferred.
   - Audit log export to their SIEM (Splunk) with token-level mapping (they want correlation to request IDs).

2) Predictable latency and throughput
   - Peak: 120 concurrent sessions (chat-style, 1–3 tokens/sec per session), avg request size ~350 tokens.
   - SLO: p95 latency < 300ms for short-turn prompts (<200 tokens) during steady state.
   - Want a baked-in fallback policy: if dedicated pool saturated, route to a cheaper quantized variant with graceful truncation.

3) Embeddings + semantic search
   - Will index 18M documents (financial statements, contracts). Embedding model must be consistent (no silent model swaps).
   - Concern re: embedding drift after quantization/optimizations — they will want evaluation harness and deterministic version pinning.

4) Operational expectations
   - They require runbook + playbook for node failures and noisy-neighbor scenarios.
   - Automatic alert to their PagerDuty on any scaling fallback or model downgrade.

Gotchas / red flags observed during call:
- KMS: They insisted on a single CMK with limited key rotation windows (security policy). Need to confirm compatibility with our key-wrapping strategy (we currently re-wrap session keys with a transient key in private deployments).
- VPC peering vs. PrivateLink: Their infra team prefers VPC peering for latency, but we usually recommend PrivateLink for cross-account control. Need to verify whether peering will break our metrics collection (it can limit flow logs for the control plane).
- Huge embedding corpus: 18M docs will require sharded nearest-neighbor index; our current recommended infra uses hybrid HNSW + compressed vectors. Need to check memory footprint with 8-bit quantized embeddings and expected recall SLA.
- Tokenization mismatch: they use legacy tokenization for some upstream NLP pipelines (custom tokenizer). Could cause prompt length accounting mismatch; ask if they can migrate to standard BPE or if we need to accept raw UTF-8 text and do on-the-fly token mapping (complex).

Technical notes (me to team):
- Baseline infra suggestion: 4 x A10g or 6 x T4 (depending on availability) for initial dedicated pool; aim for CPU/GPU split for batching/encoding. Recommend starting with 4 GPUs and vertical autoscale triggers at 60% utilization.
- Embedding index: recommend starting with 128-d quantized vectors (we can test 8-bit PQ) and staged recall tests. Create eval job: sample 50k queries across different doc types (contracts vs statements) to measure degradation.
- Caching: heavy reuse expected for identical contract templates — propose prefix KV caching and a per-tenant LRU for embeddings. Need to validate cache eviction policies with their legal doc churn frequency (they estimated ~2% daily doc turnover).
- Monitoring hooks: Must expose token-level metrics and produce a joinable request_id in logs for their SIEM. Need to confirm whether their Splunk ingestion accepts JSON with custom fields or we need to JMS->S3 drop.

Unresolved questions to confirm with customer (actionable):
- Derek: can you share the CMK ARN and rotation window policy? (security ask)
- Jason: are you ok with PrivateLink or do you require VPC peering? If peering, we need control-plane fallback explained.
- Nora: what's the expected QPS during peak (they said 120 sessions but we need ops-level RPS numbers).
- Embeddings: can they accept occasional reindex windows or do they insist on near-zero downtime? If zero downtime, we need a blue/green index swap plan.

Action items (owner, due):
- (Elena) Draft preliminary private-deploy topology (AWS account boundaries, subnets, required IAM roles) — due 2026-03-05.
- (Miguel) Validate KMS flow: can we honor their CMK with our wrap/unwarp flow and document any drift — due 2026-03-06.
- (Priya) Produce an incident runbook template showing scaling fallback and PD alert payload — due 2026-03-07.
- (Rivermark / Jason) Provide sample payloads for tokenization (2–3 representative documents) and CMK ARN — requested 2026-03-04.

Quick proposal sketch to send next:
- 2-phase onboarding: Phase A (Proof-of-Concept, 4 GPUs, limited dataset 100k docs, basic SIEM hook, test CMK integration) — 6 weeks.
- Phase B (Scale + go-live): expand to 6–8 GPUs, full embedding index roll, HA control-plane (PrivateLink preferred), final SLA negotiation.
- Pricing: give them a draft reserved-capacity quote (6-month ramp). Leave wiggle room for quantization work and reindexing ops.

Notes to self:
- Keep embedding eval harness isolated in their account if possible (or deliver reproducible docker image).
- Check existing PR #321 (linked) — Miguel started a KMS compatibility patch that might speed work.
- Document any deviations from standard private-deploy quickstart in Confluence page linked above.

Meeting follow-up: send a concise one-pager to Nora/Jason summarizing the two-phase plan + immediate asks (CMK ARN, sample payloads, preferred connectivity). Attach draft runbook and the estimated GPU baseline.

Free-form capture / scribbles (raw):
- "If they insist on single CMK -> may need to accept longer rotation windows or write policy exceptions."
- "Embedding recall vs cost tradeoff: we might push for hybrid recall where legal contracts get higher-dim vectors."
- "Possible early win: show them a 1k-doc demo with instant search to build confidence on recall."

End notes: keep this doc lightweight. Move finalized architecture to Confluence after sign-off.

-- Elena
